The `getBoundingClientRect()` data for `root>plain>pin` directly shows where the element renders on screen. It reports `x=10 y=10`, which is the viewport-relative position of the top-left corner. Since `root>plain` has `position: static`, it doesn't create a new positioning context, so the absolutely positioned `pin` element positions relative to `root` (which has `position: relative`). The `left: 10px` and `top: 10px` values place it at those coordinates within the root's coordinate system.

ANSWER: 10,10
